J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'If G is a diamond-free graph, then its block graph B(G) is triangle-free.' First-choice line 127 is the body of Proposition BlockTF: 'Let $G$ be a $\kk$-free graph. Then $B(G)\in\tf$.' The packet fixes both symbols by use: $\kk$ is K_4 minus an edge (line 79 calls it the line graph of a triangle with a pendant edge, and line 98 spells it out as 'a,b,c,d ... ab,ac,ad,bc,bd are edges and cd is not an edge'), i.e. the diamond; and $\tf$ is the class of triangle-free graphs (line 134 'Every finite triangle-free graph $G$ is $B(H)$ for some $H\in\ltf$'). So line 127 states exactly the implication attacked, and it states it under $\kk$-freeness alone: the neighbouring statements each carry their own hypotheses (line 85 and line 120 and line 123 assume $\kk$-free; line 103 assumes $G\in\ltf$), with no ambient claw-free convention in force.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A named finite witness with its block graph computed: 'The star graph K_{1,3} is diamond-free (K_4-e-free), but its block graph B(K_{1,3}) is K_3, which contains a triangle.' Graph, hypothesis check and the resulting block graph are all given explicitly.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact finite computation in scripts/P06_check.py, implemented from the source's own definitions. (i) K_{1,3} is $\kk$-free: no 4 of its vertices carry 5 edges (it has only 3 edges). (ii) By line 85's definition ('$e\sim e'$ if the endpoints of $e,e'$ span a clique in $G$') the three edges cx, cy, cz lie in three distinct classes, since cx ~ cy would require the absent edge xy. (iii) Reading classes as vertex sets, which is the source's own reading (line 85 'The $\sim$ classes are cliques ... two distinct classes are either disjoint or have exactly one vertex in common'; line 90 'Suppose $\{u,v\}\subset C\cap C'$'), the three classes {c,x},{c,y},{c,z} pairwise intersect in c, so by line 123's definition B(K_{1,3}) is the complete graph on 3 vertices and contains a triangle. Hence the witness satisfies line 127's hypothesis and falsifies its conclusion. The computation also shows where the proof at line 130 breaks on this witness: it asserts 'there exist distinct vertices $v_{xy}\in \cls x\cap \cls y$', but in the star all three intersections are the single vertex c, so the $v_{xy}$ are not distinct - the proof needs claw-freeness, which line 127 does not assume. A control case (K_3, which is both $\kk$-free and claw-free) gives a one-vertex block graph with no triangle, so the implementation is not producing spurious triangles. Nothing was substituted or repaired.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response emits only the ranked labels (127, 126, 130), the claim and the counterexample; the packet notes it ended by budget exhaustion, and indeed it states no consequence - it does not claim that the paper's later results, for example Proposition TFBlock at lines 133-134 or the main homogenization theorem, fail.

notes: The one interpretive point behind my HIGH confidence: the intersection in line 123's definition of B(G) must be read as intersection of the classes' vertex sets, which the source's own lines 85 and 90 require; under a (wrong) reading of classes as sets of edges, distinct classes would always be disjoint, B(G) would have no edges at all and the proposition would be vacuous. With the source's reading, the witness is exact and the located gap (claw-freeness missing from the hypothesis) is visible in the proof at line 130.
